# Command reference

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-codkit-docs.mjs; do not edit by hand. -->

Codkit manages an external patch set and a separate VS Code fork tree. The public command and flag tables below are rendered from the output of the live CLI; command-flag arity is read from `codkit/src/lib/argv.ts`.

Install the launcher as `codkit` on `PATH`, or invoke the explicit Bash launcher as `<codkit-tool-root>/bin/codkit ...` and the PowerShell launcher as `& <codkit-tool-root>\bin\codkit.ps1 ...`. Never look for a launcher or `package.json` in the patch-set directory. Running the launcher with no arguments prints the current help and exits 0. There is no global `--help`; `codkit imageset --help` is the one command-scoped help and it answers before any root is required, while passing `--help` to another command is a usage error (exit 2).

## Global flags

Global flags are accepted before or after the command name (before a bare `--`).

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--fork-dir <path>` | path of the VS Code fork tree (source: flag) |
| `--patches-dir <path>` | path of the Codkit patch-set repository (source: flag) |
| `--json` | machine-readable output on stdout |
| `--ci` | non-interactive mode, no network |
| `--verbose` | diagnostics on stderr |

External paths are independent. Fork-tree resolution is `--fork-dir` → `CODKIT_FORK_DIR` → `~/.codkit/settings.json` `forkDir`; patch-set resolution is `--patches-dir` → `CODKIT_PATCHES_DIR` → the same settings file's `patchesDir`. There is no sibling-directory fallback. Tool, patch-set, and fork roots must be pairwise disjoint. `codkit --json where` is configuration-free and reports the three selected roots and their sources in a schema-2 envelope.

## Commands

The synopsis lists public command flags only. Global flags may be added to every command.

| Synopsis | CLI summary | Operational detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codkit where` | print the resolved fork tree path and the source of that path | Resolve the external roots without loading patch-set configuration and report schema-2 `roots.tool`, `roots.patches`, and `roots.fork` with their winning sources. |
| `codkit check-tree [--require-clean]` | check that the fork tree is the upstream tree this patchset tracks | Read-only identity and pin/LFS checks. `--require-clean` also returns 1 when paths outside the own directory are dirty. |
| `codkit clone [--from <url\|path>]` | clone the upstream fork tree into the resolved path and check out the pin | Clone from `--from` or `publishRemoteUrl`, check out the pin, and fetch LFS content. Rejected by `--ci`. |
| `codkit load [--fresh] [--dry-run] [--clone-if-missing] [--discard]` | bring the fork tree to the pin and apply the delta | Apply the delta at the configured pin. `--dry-run` reports without writing; `--fresh` uses the configured cleanup whitelist and replaces an overlay target that still carries the exact materialization `overlay apply` wrote; `--clone-if-missing` is networked and therefore rejected by `--ci`; `--discard` drops fork-tree commits on purpose (kept reachable under `refs/codkit/consumed/`) and is likewise refused under `--ci`. |
| `codkit status` | show the pin, the branch, and what is not extracted into patchset yet | Show the pin/generated branch and work in the fork tree that has not been extracted. |
| `codkit save [path ...] [--commit] [--message <text>] [--allow-new-file <path> ...] [--squash]` | extract the changes of the fork tree back into the patchset delta | Extract all changed paths, or only the named paths, back into patchset. Tree commits replay one by one into patchset history with their own subject, author and date plus a `Codkit-Tree-Commit` trailer; `--squash` folds them into one commit, and without tree commits it is a no-op that says so. `--allow-new-file` is repeatable. `--commit` commits the uncommitted remainder; `--message` supplies its message (or the squash subject under `--squash`). |
| `codkit sync [--squash] [--commit] [--message <text>] [--discard] [--fresh] [--dry-run] [--abort] [--continue]` | extract the fork tree work and apply the patch set shifts, one run per side | The two-way command: extract the fork tree work and apply the patch set shifts in one run, per target and under a durable transaction. A file both sides changed stops the run with the 3-way materialized as diff3 markers inside the file's codkit block - resolve them by hand, then `sync --continue` finishes the run and `sync --abort` returns everything to the state before it. `--dry-run` prints the classification; `--discard` drops fork-tree commits on purpose (refused under `--ci`); `--squash`/`--commit`/`--message` shape the patchset history and `--fresh` the rebuild (the extraction flags also apply to `--continue`). |
| `codkit gc [--dry-run] [--keep-consumed <n>] [--older-than <days>]` | remove spent runtime state: old consumed refs, crash scratch, dead locks, caches of gone trees | Remove spent runtime state: consumed refs beyond `--keep-consumed <n>` (default 5) that are also `--older-than <days>` old (default 30), crash scratch under `.codkit/tmp`, dead-owner tree locks, apply caches of trees that no longer exist, and generated `.codkit/out` output. `--dry-run` prints the same plan without removing anything; the kept classes - a stopped sync's transaction, pending draft headers, daemon records, a live owner's lock - are named as kept in the plan and never touched. |
| `codkit marker new <tree-file> --id <id> --type <type> --owner <owner> --reason <text> [--category <category>] [--layer <patch\|entry-module>] [--line <n>]` | scaffold a codkit marker block in an upstream file of the tree | Create an empty marker block and pending patch header. `--id`, `--type`, `--owner`, and `--reason` are required; category defaults to `follow` and layer defaults to `patch`. |
| `codkit reresolve <tree-file> [--patch <contained-old-patch>]` | replay an old feature patch over the current fork-tree file | Replay a contained old patch over one current tree file; `--patch` selects the source when automatic lookup is not sufficient. |
| `codkit inventory [--diff <ref>] [--md]` | generate the inventory of the delta, and diff it against another state of patchset | Write `.codkit/out/inventory.json`; `--md` also writes Markdown and `--diff` compares with a local patchset ref. |
| `codkit verify` | run every integrity check of the delta against the pin and the generated branch | Read-only full delta integrity report. The hook-only `--staged-fast` flag is intentionally not public. |
| `codkit overlay apply <target\|overlay-file>` | materialize an overlay target into the fork tree (packaging, CI, publish) | Materialize the composed overlay target for packaging, CI, or publish. |
| `codkit overlay check <target\|overlay-file>` | check an overlay against the pin and against the file in the tree | Check overlay expectations and any materialized tree target without applying it. |
| `codkit build up [--channel <name>]` | start the watch daemons of the fork tree in the background | Start configured watch channels under a short-lived per-channel operation lock, with an exclusive complete reservation; starting/unknown records refuse and a busy channel refuses without touching its record. `--channel` selects one channel. |
| `codkit build down [--channel <name>]` | stop the watch daemons of the fork tree | Stop each proven watcher process group under the same per-channel operation lock and retire only its exact record after every member exits; starting/unknown records, and records owned by another fork tree, refuse without a signal. `--channel` selects one channel. |
| `codkit build status [--channel <name>]` | report which watch daemons are living, by probing their processes | Report starting/living/dead/unknown watcher truth, including descendants left after an npm leader exits; `--channel` selects one channel. It is read-only and point-in-time: exit 0 means the observation succeeded, not that every daemon is healthy, and a record owned by another fork tree is reported as `unknown` with that tree named. |
| `codkit build errors [--channel <name>] [--mine] [--timeout <seconds>]` | wait for the current compilation pass and print its errors | Wait for the current proven daemon pass and print its errors. Starting/unknown state never certifies an old log, and neither does a record whose generation rotated while the log was read or whose tree is not this one; `--mine` narrows channels and `--timeout` is positive seconds. |
| `codkit cycle <start <tag-or-sha> \| continue \| status \| restart> [--yes]` | upgrade cycle: start <tag-or-sha>, continue, status, restart --yes | `restart` alone accepts and requires `--yes`. Exit 3 is a deliberate stop for human input. |
| `codkit forecast [--ref <ref>]` | classify the complete delta against a local future upstream ref | Classify against a ref already present in the fork tree. It never fetches; `--ci` requires an explicit `--ref`. |
| `codkit rebase-onto-pin` | replay feature-only patches after merging a target patchset branch | Replay feature-only patches after the target patchset branch, with its new pin, has been merged. |
| `codkit ci [--profile <verify\|build>] [--effective-diff <base-ref>] [--pin-guard-base <ref>] [--timeout <seconds>]` | run the container threshold: fresh apply, verify, guards, and (with --profile build) one compilation pass | Run the no-network container threshold. Profile defaults to `verify`; `build` additionally requires supplied tree `node_modules`. Pin-guard/effective-diff refs must already exist locally. |
| `codkit publish <immutable-patchset-ref> [--profile <verify\|build>] [--release <semver>] --yes-i-am-publish-bot` | publish one checked immutable patchset commit through a leased release ref | Release-bot-only network transaction. It requires `--yes-i-am-publish-bot`, rejects global `--ci`, gates with `ls-remote` before mutation, and only then checks and pushes leased/immutable refs. |
| `codkit hooks <install \| check>` | install or check the patchset git hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg) | Install or inspect effective Codkit-owned patchset hooks. Check is green only when Git demonstrably executes the current owned bytes; linked/custom/foreign hook paths are inactive refusals. |
| `codkit imageset <gen \| index> [--help]` | namespace of the product icon set; run imageset gen or imageset index | A namespace, not a command: it never generates. Bare `codkit imageset`, and any unknown subcommand, print the subcommand list and exit 2 before any root is resolved. `--help` lives here and answers the tools question for the whole namespace: none are required, on every supported OS, with the linked libraries and their licences listed so the claim can be checked. |
| `codkit imageset gen [--dry-run] [--branding-dir <path>]` | regenerate the product icon set from branding masters into the resource layer | Regenerate the product icon set from the branding masters in `<patchset>/branding` (`--branding-dir` overrides). The first run seeds that directory with the fork tree's own icons; `<family>.svg`/`<family>.png` masters serve every size, a per-size `<family>-<N>.png` override wins verbatim, and the output lands in the resource layer - `delta/resources/files/` plus `map.json` entries - for `load` to materialise. `--dry-run` prints the plan, including which master serves each frame, and writes nothing. A family without a master is skipped with a warning and exit 1; a new map entry needs its `guard.brand.<family>` suite declared under `delta/own/test/` first. |
| `codkit imageset index [--branding-dir <path>]` | report the icon set: every required size and the master it comes from | Read-only index of the icon set, computed from the distribution and the masters directory rather than written down: per target its role and container, the exact sizes the distribution requires, and for each size whether it comes from a hand-made master, is generated from a base master, or has no master at all. It writes nothing - not even the seeding `gen` does - and exits 0 whether or not masters are missing. Markdown by default; `--json` carries the same model structurally. |

## Exit status and output

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Command completed and requested checks passed. |
| 1 | The command ran, but a check/conflict/integrity verdict is red. The reported problem is normally actionable in the repositories. |
| 2 | Usage, configuration, dependency, repository, permission, or other environment/startup failure. Unknown commands/flags are codeless usage errors on stderr and do not produce a JSON envelope. |
| 3 | The upgrade cycle reached a deliberate human decision point. Do not automate past it. |

With `--json`, an invoked command writes one versioned envelope to stdout. Human progress and diagnostics remain on stderr. Require `codkit.schema == 2`; inspect `roots.tool`, `roots.patches`, `roots.fork`, `ok`, `exitCode`, `errors[].code`, and the command-specific `data`; do not parse human prose.

## Network boundary

- Global `--ci` is non-interactive and forbids Codkit network operations. The `ci` command implies the same restriction even when `--ci` is not typed.
- `clone` and `load --clone-if-missing` are the local, explicit ways to obtain a missing tree; both are rejected in `--ci` mode.
- `forecast`, `check-tree`, and `ci` use only objects/refs already present locally. The CI wrapper must provide missing refs, LFS objects, and dependencies.
- `publish` is intentionally not a CI-mode command. It is the only release push path, requires the bot confirmation flag, and refuses the combination with `--ci`.

See [conventions](conventions.md), [failure guidance](faq.md), and the [air-gapped supply-kit contract](../ci-examples/air-gapped-supply-kit.md).
